edges.description: Loss of PWWP H3K36me2/3 tethering allows mutant DNMT3A to hypermethylate Polycomb-regulated developmental loci.
DNMT3A dysfunction perturbs developmental transcriptional programs required for normal cortical progenitor maintenance and neurodevelopment.
Abnormal developmental epigenetic regulation contributes to microcephaly and premature cranial suture ossification.
DNMT3A developmental epigenetic dysregulation is associated with the opposing-growth HESJAS phenotype that includes growth failure.
Neurodevelopmental progenitor disruption produces profound global developmental delay.
Premature depletion of neural progenitor pools reduces cortical cell number and brain size.
Impaired cranial growth leads to microcephaly.
Abnormal cranial morphogenesis can lead to premature cranial suture fusion.
Abnormal craniofacial growth and morphogenesis produce facial dysmorphic features.
DNA hypermethylation at Polycomb-marked and lineage-specific genes impairs stem cell maintenance and differentiation capacity across multiple tissue lineages.
Hypermethylation of Polycomb-regulated neurodevelopmental loci in neural progenitor cells biases differentiation away from self-renewal.

Reduced stem cell output and lineage skewing compromise tissue regenerative capacity, contributing to the growth delay phenotype. The potential role of stem cell dysfunction in age-related hematological, bone, and metabolic complications remains to be characterized clinically in HESJAS.
Premature depletion of stem/progenitor pools reduces somatic cell number and drives proportionate short stature (microcephalic dwarfism).
Reproduces de novo DNA hypermethylation at Polycomb-regulated developmental loci (including Hoxc13, Sox1, and genome-wide NPC hypermethylated DMRs) in vivo in mouse cerebral cortex and liver.
Models DNMT3A gain-of-function-driven multilineage stem cell dysfunction, reduced somatic and brain growth, and age-associated DNA methylation changes.

nodes.description: No targeted epigenetic therapy is established; clinical management is supportive and multidisciplinary, encompassing neurodevelopmental habilitation, growth monitoring, and craniofacial/neurosurgical evaluation when craniosynostosis is present. Because cranial vault surgical reconstruction for craniosynostosis is generally performed within the first year of life, operative intervention may be deferred in favor of clinical suture monitoring during follow-up in older children with severe developmental delay.

nodes.description: Region-specific DNA hypermethylation driven by DNMT3A gain-of-function causes dysfunction of stem/progenitor cells across multiple lineages. This manifests as reduced stem cell output and abnormal lineage skewing, compromising tissue regenerative capacity and total somatic cell number. In model systems, this mechanism is implicated in age-related hematological, bone, and metabolic dysfunction, though the extent to which these age-related phenotypes manifest clinically in pediatric HESJAS patients remains incompletely characterized.
